questions.q: How many ways can 5 distinct books be arranged on a shelf?
In how many ways can a president, vice-president, and secretary (three distinct roles) be chosen from a club of 12 members?
How many distinct arrangements are there of the letters in the word APPLE?
questions.answer: There are 5 letters with the letter P repeated twice: \(\frac{5!}{2!}=\frac{120}{2}=60\).

sections.heading: Part III — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: The bar chart shows the distribution of grades in a class of 37 students. Find the probability that a randomly selected student earned a grade of A or B, as a percent to the nearest whole percent.
Using the same bar chart, find the probability that a randomly selected student scored a C or D grade, as a percent to the nearest whole percent.
Find the coefficient of \(x^3y^2\) in the expansion of \((x+y)^5\).
questions.answer: The term is \(\binom{5}{2}x^3y^2\), so the coefficient is \(\binom{5}{2}=10\).
questions.explanation: The term is \(\binom{5}{2}x^3y^2\), so the coefficient is \(\binom{5}{2}=10\).

questions.q: In the expansion of \((2x-1)^4\), find the coefficient of \(x^2\).
questions.answer: The general term is \(\binom{4}{k}(2x)^{4-k}(-1)^k\). For \(x^2\), \(4-k=2\Rightarrow k=2\): \(\binom{4}{2}(2x)^2(-1)^2=6(4x^2)=24x^2\). The coefficient is \(24\).
questions.explanation: The general term is \(\binom{4}{k}(2x)^{4-k}(-1)^k\). For \(x^2\), \(4-k=2\Rightarrow k=2\): \(\binom{4}{2}(2x)^2(-1)^2=6(4x^2)=24x^2\). The coefficient is \(24\).

questions.q: A data set is normally distributed with mean \(100\) and standard deviation \(15\). What percent of values lie between \(70\) and \(130\)?
questions.answer: \(70\) and \(130\) are each \(2\) standard deviations from the mean (\(100\pm30\)). By the 68-95-99.7 rule, about \(95\%\) of values lie in this range.
questions.explanation: \(70\) and \(130\) are each \(2\) standard deviations from the mean (\(100\pm30\)). By the 68-95-99.7 rule, about \(95\%\) of values lie in this range.

questions.q: For the same distribution (mean \(100\), standard deviation \(15\)), find the approximate percentage of values greater than \(115\).
questions.answer: \(115\) is \(1\) standard deviation above the mean. About \(68\%\) of values lie within \(1\) standard deviation, so \(34\%\) lie between the mean and \(115\). Since \(50\%\) lie above the mean, the percentage above \(115\) is \(50\%-34\%=16\%\).
questions.explanation: \(115\) is \(1\) standard deviation above the mean. About \(68\%\) of values lie within \(1\) standard deviation, so \(34\%\) lie between the mean and \(115\). Since \(50\%\) lie above the mean, the percentage above \(115\) is \(50\%-34\%=16\%\).

questions.answer: From the bar chart, the number of students who prefer apples is 15. The number of students who prefer bananas is 10. The total number of students who prefer apples and bananas is the sum of these two values: 15 + 10 = 25.

questions.q: Events \(A\) and \(B\) are mutually exclusive, with \(P(A) = 2/7\) and \(P(B) = 3/8\). Find \(P(A \mathrm{\ or\ } B)\).

questions.answer: Mutually exclusive events: \(P(A \mathrm{\ or\ } B) = P(A)+P(B) = 2/7+3/8 = 37/56\).

Show that the binomial distribution approaches Poisson as \(n\rightarrow\infty\), \(p\rightarrow0\), \(np=\lambda\) fixed.
questions.answer: Applying Probability & Statistics principles, Poisson limit theorem. Therefore, the verified correct option is \(\binom{n}{k}p^k(1-p)^{n-k}\rightarrow\frac{e^{-\lambda}\lambda^k}{k!}\) — use \((1-\lambda/n)^n\rightarrow e^{-\lambda}\).
questions.explanation: Applying Probability & Statistics principles, Poisson limit theorem. Therefore, the verified correct option is \(\binom{n}{k}p^k(1-p)^{n-k}\rightarrow\frac{e^{-\lambda}\lambda^k}{k!}\) — use \((1-\lambda/n)^n\rightarrow e^{-\lambda}\).
